chunks: Say: "Call those whom you imagine to be gods besides Him; yet they have no power to relieve you of any distress or to avert it."
ai.seo_question: What is the proof of the impotence of false gods in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is pivotal for establishing the ontological distinction between the Creator and the created, often cited to refute the Shirk of those who attribute independent power to saints or angels. It underscores that while intercession (Tawassul) is valid, it is solely by God's permission, as false deities lack the inherent ability to remove harm or effect change. This reinforces the principle of Tawhid al-Af'al, where all agency ultimately returns to Allah alone.
